title: The Icosaxes Hexa: Bloom, Bud and Seed
description:
In short. The DICTO Hexa (#18) is eight DICTO Jewels that pass into each other until they close into one block. DICTO asked for the same move with icosahedral symmetry. Twenty Icosaxes, DICTO's golden truncated octahedra (#48), placed on the corners of a dodecahedron and slid towards the centre first touch as a cage with twelve windows (at distance φ²√3/2); at exactly 1/φ of that distance the windows close into a shell round a hollow; at exactly one third the hollow fills and the shell becomes one solid (with Lotus Jewel Axes: at 1/φ³). Proved exactly. In the lattice, eight Icosaxes round an Unborn Axes make one solid (the same as nine Icosaxes passing through each other, along the whole golden bond from Kelvin onwards), and these blocks form a Kagome network in which every Icosaxes is shared by exactly two blocks; keyed with Tricaps, its piece has volume exactly φ².

The idea is DICTO's; the names are DICTO's working names. Computation and proof with Claude (Anthropic); a first draft by a local open model (gpt-oss-120b), checked line by line. Licence CC BY-SA 4.0. More at dictospheres.com.
notes: #59 in DICTO's numbering (dictospheres.com). The idea is DICTO's; Icosaxes, Unborn Axes, Lotus Jewel Axes, Dodecaxes and Tricap are DICTO's names; Icosaxes Bloom, Bud and Seed (Lotus Jewel Bloom, Bud and Seed), Icosaxes Hexa, Lotus Hexa, Keyaxes and Icosaxes Kagome are DICTO's working names.
